written.myAnswer: Examples of contact forces include friction, normal force, air resistance (drag), tension, and an applied push or pull.

Friction opposes relative motion or the tendency of surfaces to move relative to each other. If a block on a table is pushed but the push is not enough to make it slide, static friction balances the push and the block remains at rest. Once the block slides, kinetic friction acts between the surfaces and opposes the sliding motion. Static friction acts between surfaces at rest relative to each other; kinetic friction acts between surfaces sliding relative to each other.

(a) 0.5 m s⁻²
(b) 2.5 m s⁻¹, assuming the block starts from rest.
